questions.question: Wind noise can cause hearing damage?

options.text: It is easy to get used to.
It can permanently damage your hearing.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can permanently damage your hearing.
questions.explanation: Long-term exposure to wind noise can permanently damage your hearing. Wear ear plugs or other hearing protection when riding.

questions.question: What material provides the best protection for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather or sturdy synthetic materials provide the best protection for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what should riders do with their mirrors?

options.text: Only the lead rider should check them.
Do not check them because they distract you.

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often to watch the riders behind you and make sure the group stays together.

questions.question: When buying a motorcycle helmet, what should concern you most?
questions.explanation: Protection should be your top concern when buying a motorcycle helmet.

questions.question: What separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction?
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Solid white lines mean you cannot pass. Dashed white lines mean you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: If your motorcycle weaves over rain grooves or bridge gratings, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get across faster.
Exaggerate the zigzag to alert other drivers.
Keep a steady speed and ride straight across.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a steady speed and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Keep a steady speed and go straight across the grooves or gratings. Trying to correct the weave by zigzagging is more dangerous.

questions.question: Before riding, what should the throttle do when you release it?
questions.explanation: The throttle should snap back when you release it. The clutch should feel tight and smooth.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: It is not needed if you have a windshield.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face. A windshield alone is not enough protection.

questions.question: What material should riding gloves be made of?
questions.explanation: Riding gloves should be made of leather or a similar durable material for grip and protection.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Sudden changes in speed or direction can cause a skid on a slippery surface. Accelerate, shift, turn, and brake smoothly.

questions.question: Choose a lane position that:

options.text: Hides you from other road users.
Places you directly next to another vehicle.

questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that helps you avoid road hazards. Always keep safe space around your motorcycle.

questions.question: As a rider, you can reduce accident risk by:

options.text: Not using turn signals so other drivers won't be distracted.

questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible, use turn signals, keep safe distance, look ahead 12 seconds, watch for hazards, and stay ready to react.

questions.question: When entering a turn, you should:

options.text: Take the motorcycle out of gear.

questions.explanation: Change gears before entering a turn. If you must change gears while turning, do it smoothly.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign is on the rear of slow-moving vehicles traveling under 25 mph, such as farm equipment or horse-drawn vehicles.

questions.question: To be more visible to other drivers, you should:
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors while riding so others can see you. This works day or night.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They show traffic laws for that area. This sign means right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: Do not ride directly next to another vehicle because:

options.text: Another driver may want to use your lane to pass.
You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
You may have access to escape routes.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous because you may be in their blind spot. The driver won't see you. Also, that vehicle could block your escape route if hazards appear.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions coming up. This sign warns that a stop sign is ahead.

questions.question: To reduce crash risk, you should:
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible, use turn signals, keep safe distance, look 12 seconds ahead, find hazards, and be ready to react.

questions.question: When riding, your feet should be:
questions.explanation: Keep your feet on the footrests while riding to maintain good balance.
